original_question: Does every polygon admit at least one periodic orbit for the symplectic billiard dynamical system?
target_in_paper: Serge Tabachnikov, Problem 3, Question 2: "Does every polygon have a periodic orbit?" in the discussion of polygonal symplectic billiards.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact existence problem almost verbatim: it asks whether every polygon, for the polygonal symplectic billiard dynamics, has at least one periodic orbit. It also correctly asks only for existence of one periodic orbit, not for full periodicity of all orbits.
missing_details: The paper is about polygonal symplectic billiards in the plane, not symplectic billiards for arbitrary smooth tables or in higher dimensions.

The relevant dynamics is the polygonal symplectic billiard map on oriented chords, defined as the polygonal analogue of the planar symplectic reflection law described in Problem 3 and Fig. 7; periodicity is with respect to that map.
A faithful stand-alone version should avoid adding assumptions not stated here, such as convexity, rationality of angles, genericity, or smoothness conditions on the polygon.

The question is strictly an existence question for at least one periodic orbit for each polygon, not a classification of possible periods and not the stronger Question 1 about polygons for which all symplectic billiard orbits are periodic.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or quantifier of the form "for all sufficiently large m" occurs in this problem; the hidden definitions are dynamical, not algebraic.
refined_question: For a planar polygon P, consider its polygonal symplectic billiard map on oriented chords (the polygonal analogue of the symplectic reflection law in Fig. 7). Must this dynamical system always admit at least one periodic orbit?
justification: The draft is targeting the correct place in the paper: Serge Tabachnikov's Problem 3 on symplectic billiards. There the paper first introduces planar symplectic billiards as a dynamical system on oriented chords of an oval, states that polygonal symplectic billiards are defined similarly, and recalls examples of polygons for which all orbits are periodic. It then asks exactly, as Question 2, whether every polygon has a periodic orbit. Since the official formulation is already very short, the only necessary sharpening is to make explicit that the question concerns the polygonal symplectic billiard map in the plane and that "periodic orbit" means periodic under that map. Nothing in the paper's formulation adds extra hypotheses such as convexity or genericity, so those should not be inserted.
